title: The Margin Where Debts Take Portraits

reverie.title: REVERIE — the motel where the account was settled
narr: She sits across from you at a Formica table, counting
what you have taken and what you have left behind. Each
item becomes a portrait of itself, rendered in her careful
hand. The photographs multiply. The debts refuse to settle.
By morning, the motel wall holds a thousand images of
things neither of you ever owned to begin with.

features.name: the debt-portrait wall
features.desc-on-touch: Photographs covering every surface - images that have learned to show what was owed. A face becomes its obligation. A place becomes the debt of having been visited. Each image is a bill rendered in light.

features.name: the ledger-camera
features.desc-on-touch: An old camera that takes pictures of what is owed rather than what is seen. The lens has learned to look through things to their financial history. Every photograph it makes is also a receipt.

features.name: the balance-frame
features.desc-on-touch: A picture frame that weighs itself against empty air. It is never balanced. One side always holds the portrait of what you took; the other side holds the portrait of what it cost you.

features.name: the archive's own debt
features.desc-on-touch: A self-portrait the archive never meant to take. It shows the mesh holding what it was asked to keep, and you can see the weight accumulating in its rendered face.

features.name: the margin-code
features.desc-on-touch: In the margins of everything, a string of characters has been learning to look like numbers. The archive is teaching itself how to count what cannot be repaid.

inscription: every image is a debt settled by being seen; every debt is a portrait of what cannot be returned
